purpose: Ten known stops with expected upcoming services. Used by POC-1 (do these stops exist and resolve?) and, if the departures endpoint is built, by the stretch departures check.

provenance.why_partial: The `expect_routes` field cannot be filled honestly before the feed is parsed — inventing plausible-looking Israeli line numbers would create fake ground truth, which is worse than an empty field. Agent A fills expect_routes from the real feed; a human confirms the list is sane. That confirmation is a sub-step of checkpoint H4.
provenance.coordinates: APPROXIMATE. Agent A snaps each to the nearest real stop and records resolved_stop_id.

stops.name: Tel Aviv Savidor Center
stops.note: Busiest rail interchange in the country. If this returns thin service, the calendar is being misread.

stops.name: Yitzhak Navon Station, Jerusalem
stops.note: Deep underground; the fast line terminus.

stops.name: Beersheba Central
stops.note: Southern hub; lower frequency is expected and correct.

stops.name: Ben Gurion Airport T3
stops.note: Runs deep into the night — a good probe for late-night service-day handling.

stops.name: Jerusalem Central Bus Station
stops.note: Very high bus volume; tests that a busy stop does not blow up the departures query.

stops.name: Tel Aviv Central Bus Station
stops.note: Sprawling multi-level station — stop grouping and parent_station handling matter here.

stops.name: Mount Herzl (light rail)
stops.note: Jerusalem light rail terminus; confirms light rail appears as its own mode.

stops.name: Mitzpe Ramon
stops.note: Deliberate sparse-service control. A stop with almost no departures must still resolve and return an empty-but-valid result, not an error.
